---
title: "OLS Regression"
format: pdf
editor: visual
---

```{r}
# OLS regression of life satisfaction (stflife) on all predictors
# run 03_train_test_split.R first, working directory = repo folder
# needs: install.packages(c("dplyr", "car", "broom"))
# output: outputs/figures/models/ols_*.pdf
#         outputs/tables/ols_coefficients.csv, outputs/tables/ols_metrics.csv

library(dplyr)
library(car)    # vif(), Anova()
library(broom)  # tidy()

# ---- settings -------------------------------------------------------------
use_weights <- FALSE   # TRUE = weight the fit by anweight (the lasso script does this)

outcome <- "stflife"
predictors <- c("agea", "female", "hincfel", "activity_grp", "health", "sclmeet",
                "partner", "trstprl", "rlgdgr", "eisced", "domicil", "russian_home",
                "inprdsc", "sclact", "hhmmb", "ppltrst", "stfeco", "stfhlth",
                "aesfdrk", "ever_unemployed", "cntry", "round")

# variables treated as categories (each gets dummy variables)
cat_vars <- c("cntry", "round", "activity_grp", "domicil")

fig_dir <- "outputs/figures/models"
tab_dir <- "outputs/tables"
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(tab_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# ---- 1. load data ---------------------------------------------------------
train <- readRDS("ess_baltic_R9-R11_train.rds")
test  <- readRDS("ess_baltic_R9-R11_test.rds")

# categorical variables become factors; the test set uses the train levels
for (v in union(intersect(cat_vars, predictors),
                predictors[sapply(train[predictors], is.character)])) {
  train[[v]] <- factor(train[[v]])
  test[[v]]  <- factor(test[[v]], levels = levels(train[[v]]))
}

# fold and imputed columns are NOT used in the model
fml <- reformulate(predictors, response = outcome)
w   <- if (use_weights) train$anweight else NULL

# ---- 2. fit OLS on the training set --------------------------------------
fit <- lm(fml, data = train, weights = w)

summary(fit)
confint(fit)

# one test per variable (the summary only compares each dummy with its reference)
Anova(fit, type = 2)

# standardized coefficient = coefficient x (weighted) sd of its column,
# so variables on different scales can be compared (same idea as in the lasso script)
X   <- model.matrix(fit)[, -1]
wn  <- train$anweight / sum(train$anweight)
wsd <- apply(X, 2, function(x) sqrt(sum(wn * (x - sum(wn * x))^2)))

coef_table <- tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(std_estimate = estimate * wsd[term]) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(std_estimate)))
print(coef_table, n = Inf)

# ---- 3. checks ------------------------------------------------------------
# GVIF^(1/(2*Df)) is comparable across variables, values above ~2 deserve a look
print(vif(fit))

# ---- 4. plots -------------------------------------------------------------
# The old plots looked squashed because plot(fit) put four panels into a small
# figure. These are drawn on a bigger canvas, with small see-through points.
# In an Rmd/Quarto document add to the chunk header: fig.width=10, fig.height=8

dot <- rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.25)

diag_plots <- function(fit) {
  fv  <- fitted(fit)
  res <- residuals(fit)
  rs  <- rstandard(fit)
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))

  plot(fv, res, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = dot,
       xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residual", main = "Residuals vs fitted")
  abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)
  lines(lowess(fv, res), col = "blue", lwd = 2)

  qqnorm(rs, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = dot, main = "Normal QQ plot")
  qqline(rs, col = "red", lty = 2)

  plot(fv, sqrt(abs(rs)), pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = dot,
       xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "sqrt(|standardized residual|)",
       main = "Scale-location (spread of residuals)")
  lines(lowess(fv, sqrt(abs(rs))), col = "blue", lwd = 2)

  plot(hatvalues(fit), rs, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = dot,
       xlab = "Leverage", ylab = "Standardized residual",
       main = "Residuals vs leverage")
  abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}

# saved as a big PDF and also shown on screen
pdf(file.path(fig_dir, "ols_residuals.pdf"), width = 10, height = 8)
diag_plots(fit)
dev.off()
diag_plots(fit)

# standardized coefficients, longest bar = strongest tendency
pdf(file.path(fig_dir, "ols_coef.pdf"), width = 7, height = 8)
imp <- coef_table %>% arrange(abs(std_estimate))
par(mar = c(5, 11, 4, 2))
barplot(imp$std_estimate, names.arg = imp$term, horiz = TRUE, las = 1,
        cex.names = 0.7,
        col = ifelse(imp$std_estimate > 0, "steelblue", "tomato"),
        xlab = "Standardized coefficient (change in life satisfaction for 1 sd)",
        main = "OLS: coefficients")
abline(v = 0)
dev.off()

# ---- 5. test set performance ---------------------------------------------
# same weighted metrics as in the lasso script, so the two can be compared
wmetrics <- function(obs, pred, w) {
  c(RMSE     = sqrt(sum(w * (obs - pred)^2) / sum(w)),
    MAE      = sum(w * abs(obs - pred)) / sum(w),
    Rsquared = 1 - sum(w * (obs - pred)^2) /
                   sum(w * (obs - weighted.mean(obs, w))^2))
}

pred_test <- predict(fit, newdata = test)
range(pred_test)                                 # how far outside 0-10?
pred_test <- pmin(pmax(pred_test, 0), 10)        # cut to the 0-10 scale, like the lasso script

metrics <- rbind(
  `OLS (weighted)`   = wmetrics(test[[outcome]], pred_test, test$anweight),
  `OLS (unweighted)` = wmetrics(test[[outcome]], pred_test, rep(1, nrow(test)))
)
metrics <- data.frame(Model = rownames(metrics), round(metrics, 4), row.names = NULL)
print(metrics)

# observed vs predicted: one box of predictions for each observed answer 0-10
pdf(file.path(fig_dir, "ols_obs_pred.pdf"), width = 7, height = 5)
boxplot(pred_test ~ test[[outcome]], at = sort(unique(test[[outcome]])),
        xlim = c(-0.5, 10.5), ylim = c(0, 10),
        xlab = "Observed", ylab = "Predicted", main = "OLS: Obs vs Pred")
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
dev.off()

# ---- 6. save --------------------------------------------------------------
write.csv(coef_table, file.path(tab_dir, "ols_coefficients.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(metrics,    file.path(tab_dir, "ols_metrics.csv"),      row.names = FALSE)

# ---- 7. backward selection (optional) ------------------------------------
# removes predictors one by one while AIC improves.
# p-values after selection are too optimistic, so use them with care.
# fit_small <- step(fit, direction = "backward")
# summary(fit_small)

# 1. raw average per country (weighted)
train %>% group_by(cntry) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_swb = weighted.mean(stflife, anweight))

# 2. do effects differ by country? (compare with the original model)
fit_int <- update(fit, . ~ . + cntry:stfeco + cntry:hincfel + cntry:health)
anova(fit, fit_int)     # small p = the effects differ between countries

# 3. separate model per country (country itself is left out)
fml_nc <- reformulate(setdiff(predictors, "cntry"), response = outcome)
fits <- lapply(split(train, train$cntry), function(d) lm(fml_nc, data = d))
lapply(fits, function(m) round(coef(summary(m))[, c(1, 4)], 3))
```
